subject: Staged reservation + MAP: proposed ramp, pricing tiers, and burst terms
messages:
From: Evan Wells <evan.wells@apertureanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@apertureanalytics.com>, procure@apertureanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staged reservation idea for dedicated GPU pool (initial ask)

Karthik — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aperture is very interested in Redwood Dedicated for our inference workloads, but we need a reservation approach that matches our pilot -> production ramp and gives us room to burst during monthly batch jobs.

High-level ask: can Redwood propose a staged reservation MAP that ties discounts to committed units as we ramp, includes a modest burst allowance for seasonal runs, and a short evaluation phase so our infra team can validate latency at 1.2k tokens/sec?

Rough numbers from our side (subject to sizing):
- Pilot (month 0-2): 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (evaluation capacity)
- Ramp (month 3-6): increase to 12 GPUs
- Steady-state (month 7+): target 20 GPUs

Questions:
1) Can you offer a 3-stage pricing schedule (pilot / ramp / steady) with clear per-GPU unit rates and step discounts at milestone sign-offs?
2) What's your default burst policy (hours/month, multiplier) and can we reserve an extra burst bucket that draws from a different billing rate?
3) Term: we prefer 12 months but would consider 9 months with higher early-commit discounts.

I've attached a one-page draft MAP and our initial sizing workbook to help; procurement looped in for contract/PO requirements.

Thanks — Evan

Attachment(s): Aperture_MAP_v0.1.pdf (application/pdf), gpu_pool_sizing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Evan Wells <evan.wells@apertureanalytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_k@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged reservation idea for dedicated GPU pool (initial ask)

Evan — appreciate the clear ask and the workbook. We've sketched a staged-reservation MAP that aligns pricing and discounts to three acceptance milestones (pilot sign-off, ramp completion, steady-state). Summary below — attaching a short MAP doc with milestone checklist.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Pilot (0-2 months): 4 GPUs, evaluation rate = $12,000/GPU/month (trial discount 45% off list). Milestone: perf sign-off (latency and throughput).
- Ramp (3-6 months): commit to 12 GPUs at $9,000/GPU/month (committed discount kicks in after sign-off).
- Steady-state (7-12 months): 20 GPUs at $7,500/GPU/month with an additional 5% volume rebate if average usage >= 95% of committed capacity for 2 consecutive months.

Burst clause (proposed):
- Baseline burst allowance: 120 GPU-hours/month at 1.5x the committed per-hour rate (applies across all pools).
- Burst bucket option: customer may pre-purchase a burst bucket (e.g., 2,000 GPU-hours) billed at 1.2x per-hour committed rate and consumed first before default burst; unused burst bucket hours do not carry over.

Term/early exit:
- 12-month standard term; 9-month variant available with an additional upfront commitment fee equal to 10% of first 3 months’ committed spend.

Evaluation specifics: we can provide a 30-day pilot with access to a dedicated evaluation pool (the 4 GPUs above). The MAP milestone checklist will include: load test report, tail-latency at 99th percentile, and quality regression check against your prompt set.

Next steps: I propose a quick sync (30 min) week of Nov 30 to finalize the MAP details and agree on a close-by date for procurement/DocuSign. If that works, we'll circulate a single-sheet commercial summary and a DocuSign-ready Statement of Work.

Attachment(s): Redwood_APTR_MAP_proposal.pdf (application/pdf)

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Staged reservation idea for dedicated GPU pool (initial ask)

Evan — quick follow from an infra sizing perspective. I reviewed your gpu_pool_sizing.xlsx and made a couple of notes:

- For the pilot, validate with a mixed sequence length distribution (64/256/1024) so we can tune kernel selection; this is often what drives GPU count more than nominal tokens/sec.
- If you expect monthly batch jobs that peak >4x baseline, plan the burst bucket to cover the largest 2 monthly jobs (we recommend a 3,000–4,000 GPU-hour bucket for the volumes you described).
- We'll provide a canary policy for the initial roll (route 5% traffic to dedicated pilot pool, 95% to hosted). That reduces risk and verifies quality.

Operational callouts to include in MAP:
- Acceptance criteria: perf report + quality baseline check + security questionnaire sign-off (SOC2 evidence).
- Rollout timeline: 2-week canary, full ramp after acceptance.

Happy to run a short sizing workshop with your infra folks next week.

— Neha

Subject: Re: Staged reservation idea for dedicated GPU pool (initial ask) — commercial&legal notes

Evan — looping in a few commercial/legal guardrails we typically include so procurement has visibility:

1) Milestone-tied discounts: we require customer sign-off at each MAP milestone (pilot acceptance and ramp completion) to trigger the next-tier price. Sign-off can be the perf report + written approval from your infra lead.
2) Burst billing: default month-to-month burst usage billed at 1.5x; pre-purchased burst bucket priced at 1.2x and drawn first. We'll add a clause that allows one exception per year for an extra burst event (subject to capacity).
3) Termination: standard 12-month term; for 9-month term we include an early-commit fee and cap the rebate schedule.
4) Invoicing: Net 45 by default for new accounts; procurement can request Net 30 with an approved PO and reference to the signed SOW.

I've attached SOC2 evidence we can share with your security team. If Aperture needs any custom IP/data handling language (VPC/HSM/KMS), please flag asap so legal can prepare a narrow addendum.

Proposed close timeline: finalize MAP and SOW during week of Nov 30, send DocuSign by Dec 2, target signed PO by Dec 10. If you want to accelerate, we can target Dec 6 sign instead but procurement will need to confirm billing terms.

Attachment(s): SOC2-evidence.pdf (application/pdf)

— Marissa (head of commercial ops)

Thanks — this is helpful and mostly aligns with what our leadership wants. A few quick items from procurement/finance:

- Aperture is comfortable with a 12-month term at the proposed tiering, but we'd like the target close moved up. Can you confirm availability for an executive sign-off call on Dec 3 (our time) and have DocuSign ready by Dec 4?
- For burst billing, we prefer the pre-purchased burst-bucket approach (1.2x) and would like an option to top-up during Q1 without renegotiating pricing. Is that possible?
- Please confirm Net 30 invoicing once we provide a PO; finance will expect that on our side.

If you can update the single-sheet commercial and submit the DocuSign link by Dec 4, we'll aim to return a signed PO by Dec 9. Appreciate the quick turn.

— Evan
